insights.methodology: Every insight cites the specific ratio/period pair it is derived from in ratios_timeseries.json.

risk_signals.statement: NPL ratio climbed from 2.68% (FY2011) to a peak of 7.41% (FY2014), stayed elevated through FY2017 (5.79%), then steadily improved to 4.57% by FY2021 — a multi-year cycle that fully resolved rather than compounding.
CAR rose from an FY2017 low of 11.51% to a consistent 14-16% range from FY2021 onward, comfortably above the regulatory minimum throughout, even as NPL ratio fluctuated in the same period.

NPL ratio spiked to 6.85% (FY2022) and again to a series-high 7.32% (FY2024) with provisioning nearly doubling that year, but then improved sharply to 4.12% in FY2025 alongside a series-high ROE of 17.05% and EPS more than doubling (2.09 -> 4.38) — a volatile but ultimately favorable recent stretch.

Newly-sourced interim data shows FY2024's now-familiar full-year NPL/provisioning spike (see 'recent_npl_volatility_with_strong_recovery' above) was heavily front-loaded within the year: cumulative provisions reached BDT 1,947.7mn by Q1 2024 alone (vs BDT 470.0mn in Q1 2023) and BDT 3,539.8mn by H1 2024 (vs BDT 994.2mn in H1 2023), pushing H1 2024 Profit After Tax down to just BDT 740.0mn (-53% YoY) despite Profit before provisions actually being higher than a year earlier. Since full-year FY2024 PAT (BDT 4,373mn, per the existing Q4 record) ended up well above FY2023's BDT 3,486mn, roughly 83% of FY2024's full-year profit was realised in H2 2024 alone -- a pattern invisible in annual-only data and only revealed by the interim quarterly filings.

insights.historical_context: NCC Bank shows a cyclical but ultimately resilient pattern over its full 15-year public history: an early-2010s NPL climb that resolved by FY2021, followed by more volatile but shorter NPL swings in FY2022 and FY2024, each followed by improvement rather than compounding. Capital adequacy has strengthened steadily since FY2017 and remained comfortably above the regulatory minimum throughout. FY2025 stands out as the strongest year in the series on both asset quality and profitability simultaneously.
